title: Research vs Opinions Explained Simply | Marketing Management Ep 8
description:
Dev says everyone will buy Laddoo Lab. Arjun says only parents will. Two strong opinions, and zero facts. In this animated lesson, Zoya takes a short survey to school gates, gyms and offices in Bengaluru, and we use her millet laddoo brand to learn how marketing research really works.

You will see Kotler and Armstrong's textbook definition of marketing research, then watch Zoya follow their four steps live: define the problem, plan the research, collect and analyze 150 answers, and report what she found (example figures). We compare secondary data (already exists, cheap and quick) with primary data (new, made for your own question), and the three main ways to collect it: observation, surveys and experiments. Then we see each tool at work today, in a hospital, an airline, a bakery and a food delivery app. We also look at the human side honestly: research replaces guesses with facts, but it costs time and money, and a bad sample gives a wrong answer. In 1936 the Literary Digest polled over two million people and predicted the wrong US election winner, while George Gallup, with about 50,000 people, got it right.

This is Episode 8 of our Marketing Management series for MBA, BBA and commerce students.
